180 days is the front-left edge of the surface (the edge along which the ticket-size ticks 25…2500 run). Along that near edge the sheet's height above the base plate rises monotonically left to right (~39px above the plate near "50", ~50px at "100", ~84px at "250", ~122px at "500", still rising after perspective correction), and then the sheet simply ends just past the "500" label — beyond it is bare plate (floor colour), which is exactly where the three gold WITHHELD pads and the ABSENT hole-pin sit, so $1000k has no value at 180 days. The "PEAK 74% · $500k · 30 d" callout corroborates that the ridge sits in the $500k band.

The front-right edge of the plan diamond is the 180-day row (near corner = 180 d / $2500k, right corner = smallest ticket). Tracing the mesh boundary above that edge, height rises monotonically with ticket size (~0.20 at $100k, ~0.24 at $250k, ~0.29 at $500k, ~0.39 at $1000k, peaking off-option at $2500k), so the largest offered band is highest. This only came out of a pixel-level reconstruction of the axonometric mapping: the ticket axis is linear in dollars, so $100k/$250k/$500k occupy the last ~10% of the edge with their tick labels overprinted into an unreadable blob, the mesh's vertical scale does not reconcile with the z-axis ticks (24 px per 0.1 = 240 px/unit on the axis vs ~450-560 px/unit needed for the mesh to fit the stated 0.14-0.74 domain), and the 180-day edge is broken by an open cell near the 60-day boundary. Nothing in that corner is separable by eye.

Axis labels put 180 days at the near/bottom corner and 2500k there too, with 100k at the right corner, so the 180-day slice is the near-right edge. Measured against the z-axis (0.2 at y=583, 0.7 at y=464, floor 0.14 at y=597), the surface's right tip touches the right corner at y=594 (~0.15) — so 100k at 180 days is the LOWEST cell — while the peak (~0.6-0.74) sits above the opposite far corner (14 days, smallest ticket). That diagonal ridge (fast+small, slow+large) implies the largest band wins at 180 days, and since 2500k is not an option the inference lands on 1000k. Critically, the cells that would actually show this are not drawn: the whole near half of the footprint, including the (180 d, 2500k) corner, is bare background (sampled RGB 4,6,11), the mesh is a ribbon hugging only the two far edges, and each screen column carries two plan points so heights along the 180-day row are ambiguous — the caption itself says the far face needs another azimuth.

The 180-day row is the plate's front-left edge (the 25..2500 ticket ticks sit along it). The surface's front-left silhouette climbs monotonically left-to-right — from hugging the floor to a sharp corner where it stops — so win rate rises with ticket size at 180 days, and the highest DRAWN node on that edge is $500k. But that read is not available by eye: I got it by extracting the surface mask and fitting a projective map from the tick labels plus the peak drop-pole's base. Validation: the 3 gold WITHHELD blocks land exactly on nodes ($1000k/90d, $2500k/90d, $1000k/180d) with a consistent 23px marker offset; pixel-height x perspective weight at the peak node returns 74.0% vs the printed "74% $500k 30d"; and the 6 cells killed by 3 withheld + 2 absent points reproduce the printed "OBSERVED 24 cells" of 30. That calibration gives, along days=180: ~6% at $50k, ~26% at $100k, ~49% at $250k, ~68% at $500k, and the edge terminates there because $1000k/180d is the withheld block. So $1000k — the only option that could beat it — is a value the chart deliberately does not show.
